qolFindings.title: A telephone written in two-digit groups separated by spaces, with 8 or 9 digits, still has the shape of a date plus an age, so the line is left unread and the reason says it is not a telephone
qolFindings.scenario: Probe round9/r9v, readPhone false, line 'Veldor;Marta;;16;<value>'. For '02 12 34 56', '06 12 34 567', '33 12 34 56' and '3 12 34 56', DATE_SHAPE reads the first three groups as a day, a month and a two-digit year, and the optional trailing '\s+\d{1,3}' takes the last group as an age. Each value makes the line unread with 'nella colonna Telefono c’è «…», che non è un telefono'. The same number with dots or dashes ('06 12.34.56', '02-12-34-56') is ignored correctly, and so is one with 5 groups ('02 12 34 56 78'). No data is lost: the line is shown with its text and can be fixed in place. But V5F-4 says 'a telephone, even malformed or written in groups, is still ignored', and the code comment says 'a telephone in groups (02-12-34-56) has more groups'. Neither holds for space-separated pairs. This needs an assistant that ignores the prompt and fills the Telefono column.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Simplest: reword V5F-4 and the comment to 'a telephone in two-digit groups separated only by spaces may be shown as a date'. Or accept the trailing age only after a date written with separators or with a four-digit year, and add '06 12 34 56' to the corpus.
